Engineering Readiness Audit · Revision 5

Cosmic Shore

Re-run on 21 September against bleeding-edge, nine days after Revision 4. The six-week window the plan was written against closed on 11 September. Engineering kept arriving; this run corrects three claims Revision 4 got wrong; and a same-day owner report closes the largest unknown on the board — fresh builds run, multiplayer included.

Same-day addendum — 21 September, after this audit was measured

The owner reports that fresh builds have been installed and run correctly, multiplayer features included, with the note that it "needs everyday testing but it works". That closes the largest single unknown this series has carried: whether a Windows player runs at all.

It is a report, not a verdict. There is no entry in Docs/QA/RESULTS/, no build id and no log, so the project still holds one recorded verdict — from 14 August. Every figure in this document was measured before the report and none of them moves: the recording is what is missing, not the testing. R1 is re-marked 🟡 on the board rather than closed.

01 The window closed, and the plan did not notice

Revision 2 was written on 31 July with a six-week calendar path. That path ended on 11 September. Every prior audit measured the project against the plan's content; this one starts by measuring it against the plan's clock, because that is the number an investor reads first and no checkpoint has stated it.

Week one of that plan required a Steamworks partner account, the Direct fee paid, and an app record created. Tools/Steam/upload.sh still opens with the line "NOTHING HERE RUNS UNTIL THE APP EXISTS ON STEAMWORKS", and both STEAM_APPID and STEAM_DEPOTID remain unset required variables. On the repository's own evidence, week one has not happened. Weeks two through six each depend on it.

The premise that expired first

Revision 2's headline was "0 features left to build" and "feature-complete". That was true when written. Measured from the commit at 31 July to 0eef7c5b: 1,966 commits (1,535 non-merge), 19 new game-mode ids, and enabled scenes in build settings 15 → 33.

The new modes are Cleave, Wildlife Liberation, Dog Fight, The Bends, Scarab Scramble, Salvo, Switchback, Hijack, Tollway, Headlong, Breakwater, Skein, Bloomrush, Redline, Wrecking Ball, Undertow, Regatta, Broadside and Online Duel for the Cell. This is not a criticism of the work — it is uniformly high quality. It is that the thing being shipped is no longer the thing that was scoped, and every validation estimate in the plan was sized against the smaller game.

02 Three corrections to Revision 4

An audit is only worth its own accuracy. Three of Revision 4's statements do not survive re-measurement, and the first one moves the project's risk position in the right direction.

Rev 4 saidVerdictWhat the tree shows
"Nothing in CI builds a Windows player."Wrong.github/workflows/unity-ci.yml runs a weekly IL2CPP Windows player build on a self-hosted runner via CosmicShoreBuildPipeline.BuildWindowsRelease, and a Verify build output step fails the job unless CosmicShore.exe exists. The scheduled run of 17 September was green, as were 7 of the last 10. The step existed at Revision 4's own base commit. A Windows player is being built — and, per the owner report below, one has now been run.
R14 "Not started" — licence register and launch-blocker index.StaleIt landed the same day as the audit (PRs #871 and #873, merged 12 Sep from a branch since deleted). bleeding-edge carries the ✅. More importantly the one verified compliance gap — FMOD EULA clause 3 requiring an in-game "FMOD / Firelight Technologies Pty Ltd." credit on every tier — is closed and gated: Assets/Resources/CreditsManifest.asset, a release build guard, and check_credits_manifest.py --check, which passes.
"54 red + 3 amber = 57 open items" in the verification checklist.DisputedCounting section markers gives 45 red + 1 amber + 1 green = 46 open, and the checklist's own banner states 46. The two counts use different units; 57 is not reproducible. The conclusion is unaffected — none of them has been absorbed into QA — but the figure should not be quoted.

04 The blocking finding, third audit running

The quest and progression system is still not part of the build. Each sub-claim was re-measured from scratch rather than carried forward, and each one holds.

The serviceGameModeProgressionService is reached only through .Instance by 17 consumers. There is no new, no AddComponent, no Resources.Load.
Its only hostScript guid 541692fb… appears in exactly one asset: _Prefabs/MIgration_Prefabs (DELETE LATER)/PlayerDataService.prefab.
That prefabIts own guid has zero references across Assets/, ProjectSettings/ and Packages/.
The consequenceArcadeExploreView.cs:252 reads progressionService != null && !IsGameModeUnlocked(…) — a null service fails open, so every one of the 25 modes renders unlocked.

This remains correct and expected while design works the chain. It is restated because four more modes shipped into an arcade that no progression gates, and because Definition of Done #4 is unreachable however much dialogue is authored.

The invite build is the first thing anyone outside the studio will touch. Three defects sit on that surface, and none appeared in any tracker.

FindingStateDetail
Seven shipped strings the font cannot drawFixed + gatedThe UI font carries 97 glyphs with an empty fallback table, so a character outside it renders as an empty box with nothing logged. Five of the seven were on the connecting / arena-build screen — the screen every player sees on every match. Fixed this pass; Tools/Build/check_tmp_glyph_coverage.py now reads coverage off the font asset and fails CI, with 12 self-test controls.
A shipped card points at a scene that is not in the buildOpenArcadeGameCoOpWildlifeBlitz names MinigameWildlifeBlitzMultuplayerCoOp, which exists on disk but is not in build settings. Launching it from a player build fails. Separately, 20 of 51 arcade cards name scenes that do not exist at all — all legacy single-player, none on a live roster.
The STORE screen is unreachableOpenStoreScreen.cs is a real 234-line implementation with no entry in ScreenSwitcher's screens list, so the commerce de-scope branch that would mark it is dead code. Not broken — absent. Related: the Arena button is authored Available in Menu_Main.unity while the code comment describes Arena as behind a lock.
And a theme system nothing reads

UI redesign task T4 is marked DONE. UIThemeSO exists; five of its ten colour tokens and every spacing, geometry and motion token have zero C# call sites, and the only reference is one unused [SerializeField]. The tracker's own text concedes a code-only task cannot close it. Tasks T2, T5, T6, T7 and T8 remain open, and T5/T6 have been invalidated by a later style decision rather than completed.

The verdict has not changed in five weeks, and that is itself the finding. Nothing on this milestone is blocked on building something — it is blocked on one account registration, one wiring decision, and a validation pass scoped in July that has still not begun. What has changed is the denominator: the validation pass now faces 25 modes and 100 load-time cells instead of the game the plan was written against. The engineering continues to arrive well ahead of plan; the evidence that any of it works does not exist.

The one recommendation this audit will make

Every session-lane item that can be closed has been closed, and closing more of them does not move a single Definition-of-Done criterion. The next unit of work with any leverage is one person, one afternoon, one Windows build launched on one machine — it unblocks R2 and R3, converts 46 checklist rows and 68 backlog items from "never run" into data, and is the only way the B18–B23 class of defect is ever found. It has been the top of the board since Revision 3.
